summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after a fall that caused a right proximal tibia fracture. She underwent ORIF surgery and recovered well, with stable vital signs and controlled pain. Postoperatively, she developed mild wound redness attributed to hematoma, not infection, and was prescribed a short course of cephalexin as a precaution. Her chronic conditions, including HIV, hepatitis B and C, asthma, morbid obesity, and depression, remained stable. Blood pressure was managed with metoprolol, and psychiatric input led to an increase in duloxetine for mood and pain. She was transitioned to oral medications, prescribed enoxaparin for DVT prophylaxis, and discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with instructions to remain non-weight-bearing and complete her antibiotic and anticoagulant courses.
